notes.message: query listReports: truly partial absence evidence: the page over reports[..] by byId is never `complete` except for callers `exists roles[viewer, role = 'supervisor'] or exists roles[viewer, role = 'safety']` admits — the read rule `exists children[.child, parent = viewer] and exists roles[viewer, role = 'parent'] or .author = viewer and exists roles[viewer, role = 'monitor'] or exists roles[viewer, role = 'supervisor'] or exists roles[viewer, role = 'safety']` reads .author, .child, which the scan does not pin, so the server cannot tell "no more" from "more you may not read"; test.cases.jsonl: run it as a caller `exists roles[viewer, role = 'supervisor'] or exists roles[viewer, role = 'safety']` admits to expect `complete`, and expect `capped` (the default passes either) for the rest; a client shows the rows it has and treats `complete: false` as "there may be more", not an error; analyzer limitation: no verified complete form for this read (`exists children[.child, parent = viewer] and exists roles[viewer, role = 'parent']` reads a column the page does not pin and is not a `.column = viewer` party, so no pin selects its rows); keep the query and expect `capped` (check --verbose)
notes.rewrite: pin .author, .child with where equalities as well as the current equality prefix, choosing the intended scope (this narrows the answer); or read the page on the device, where the partition holds exactly what the viewer may read. As code: first declare `child: children` among listReports's arguments, then add `and .author = viewer and .child = child` to the page's where (keeping its current pins); this narrows the answer to that scope — only for a screen meant for that scope alone: every other reader the rule admits loses their rows; analyzer limitation: no verified complete form for this read: `exists children[.child, parent = viewer] and exists roles[viewer, role = 'parent']` reads a column the page does not pin and is not a `.column = viewer` party, so no pin selects its rows; keep the query as written and expect `complete: false` (`capped`; test.cases.jsonl's default passes it). This does not rule out an author-written branched query; for callers `exists roles[viewer, role = 'supervisor'] or exists roles[viewer, role = 'safety']` admits (staff), this page is decided once and answers `complete: true`; everyone else pages their own rows with complete: false — in test.cases.jsonl run it as staff to expect complete, and expect `capped` for the others
